root_idea.summary: The root centers on spoiling or deforming a form, extending to metamorphosis, loss of taste, and related deterioration; a separate lexical branch names a bow-maker and bows associated with him.
root_idea.development: Its core development runs from changing a sound or attractive form into an ugly one to physical and moral deformation, tastelessness, exhaustion-induced alteration, and figurative corruption of texts. The bow vocabulary is an attributional branch connected with the name Māṣikha.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb; the inflected QAC lemma is normalized to the classical perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To transform or metamorphose someone into a worse, fouler, or uglier form.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use denotes physical deformation or transformation. The related noun مَسْخٌ names the resulting transformed or metamorphosed state.

senses.definition: To deform a person's character, causing it to take on a vile animal-like disposition.
senses.usage_conditions: This moral sense is presented as an interpretation of the Quranic usage in 36:67, alongside the more apparent sense of physical transformation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deformed or ugly form; a person lacking beauty in appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal and adjectival usage. The term is also reported as an explanation of the epithet الدجّال in one traditional account.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alter or corrupt a text by substituting synonyms, wholly or partly, or by changing its diacritical points and thereby changing its meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the transformation or corruption of poetry and writing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a she-camel lean and injure her back through excessive fatigue and use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage for deterioration caused by exhausting use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lose or remove taste; tasteless, insipid, or more tasteless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of food, flesh, or fruit; the taste may be described as absent or as lying between sweet and bitter. The comparative form means “more tasteless.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dissolved, said of a humour.
To become lean, said of an arm or muscle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of the arm between the shoulder and elbow and of the thigh muscle, including that of a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leanness of the arm between the shoulder and elbow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun for loss of flesh in that part of the arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak and stupid; an epithet for a man with those qualities.
A bow-maker; also a bow or bows named after the bow-maker Māṣikha.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is attributed to Māṣikha of the Azd, whose name became associated with bow-making.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having little flesh in the hindquarters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical epithet applied to an animal or person.

cautions: The moral-deformation sense is explicitly attached to the Quranic usage as an interpretive possibility, while physical transformation is the more apparent reading.
